boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.8.14 וַיָּבֵ֣א אֹתִ֗י אֶל פֶּ֨תַח֙ שַׁ֣עַר בֵּית יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֖ר אֶל הַצָּפ֑וֹנָה וְהִנֵּה שָׁם֙ הַנָּשִׁ֣ים יֹֽשְׁב֔וֹת מְבַכּ֖וֹת אֶת הַתַּמּֽוּז, a third transport (“he brought me to the door of the gate of Yahweh's house” (web:Ezek.8.14)) opening the Tammuz-weeping tableau; a samekh follows this very verse (single-witness), which is disclosed as evidence that could instead argue a shorter row ending at 8:15 (see rejected alternative). The row is extended through a second transport at oshb:Ezek.8.16 וַיָּבֵ֣א אֹתִ֗י אֶל חֲצַ֣ר בֵּית יְהוָה֮ הַפְּנִימִית֒ וְהִנֵּה פֶ֜תַח הֵיכַ֣ל יְהוָ֗ה בֵּ֤ין הָֽאוּלָם֙ וּבֵ֣ין הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ כְּעֶשְׂרִ֥ים וַחֲמִשָּׁ֖ה אִ֑ישׁ אֲחֹ֨רֵיהֶ֜ם אֶל הֵיכַ֤ל יְהוָה֙ וּפְנֵיהֶ֣ם קֵ֔דְמָה וְהֵ֛מָּה מִשְׁתַּחֲוִיתֶ֥ם קֵ֖דְמָה לַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ (the sun-worshippers, “about twenty-five men… their backs toward Yahweh's temple” (web:Ezek.8.16)) because no refrain or mark separates 8:16-18 from what precedes it. Close: oshb:Ezek.8.18 וְגַם אֲנִי֙ אֶעֱשֶׂ֣ה בְחֵמָ֔ה לֹֽא תָח֥וֹס עֵינִ֖י וְלֹ֣א אֶחְמֹ֑ל וְקָרְא֤וּ בְאָזְנַי֙ ק֣וֹל גָּד֔וֹל וְלֹ֥א אֶשְׁמַ֖ע אוֹתָֽם is the wrath declaration — “I will also deal in wrath… I will not hear them” (web:Ezek.8.18) — a narrative and thematic close (the fourfold tableau's climax) rather than a recognition or utterance refrain; oshb:Ezek.9.1 opens the next scene with the loud-voiced cry that sets the executioners in motion, which is the strongest available onset-side confirmation that 8:18 is where the temple-tour proper ends.

boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.10.9 וָאֶרְאֶ֗ה וְהִנֵּ֨ה אַרְבָּעָ֣ה אוֹפַנִּים֮ אֵ֣צֶל הַכְּרוּבִים֒ אוֹפַ֣ן אֶחָ֗ד אֵ֚צֶל הַכְּר֣וּב אֶחָ֔ד וְאוֹפַ֣ן אֶחָ֔ד אֵ֖צֶל הַכְּר֣וּב אֶחָ֑ד וּמַרְאֵה֙ הָא֣וֹפַנִּ֔ים כְּעֵ֖ין אֶ֥בֶן תַּרְשִֽׁישׁ turns from the coal-taking action to a sustained physical description of the four wheels (“The appearance of the wheels was like a beryl stone” (web:Ezek.10.9)), echoing the wheel-vision of chapter 1 (the 'river Chebar' inclusio device, sweep: 8 verses book-wide, three of them at oshb:Ezek.10.15, oshb:Ezek.10.20 and oshb:Ezek.10.22). Close: oshb:Ezek.10.17 בְּעָמְדָ֣ם יַעֲמֹ֔דוּ וּבְרוֹמָ֖ם יֵר֣וֹמּוּ אוֹתָ֑ם כִּ֛י ר֥וּחַ הַחַיָּ֖ה בָּהֶֽם — “for the spirit of the living creature was in them” (web:Ezek.10.17) — ends the description with a summary clause before oshb:Ezek.10.18 resumes narrated action (the glory's departure). Both sides: as in Ezek.10.1-10.8, no parashah mark and no K/Q sit anywhere in this span (chapter 10 carries none), so the seam is argued from the shift between static description and resumed narration alone; this is disclosed as the weakest-anchored row in the part.

It is kept as its own row because it is a bytes-verifiable, self-contained descriptive block (the wheel vocabulary אוֹפַ֣ן (oshb:Ezek.10.9) and הַגַּלְגַּ֖ל (oshb:Ezek.10.13) does not recur outside 10:6-17 and 1:15-21) bounded by narrated action on both sides.

No parashah, K/Q, paseq or editorial-note disclosure applies anywhere in 10:9-17; that absence is itself disclosed.

boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.11.14 וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר, the strict word-event formula (one of the book's 39 strict-form onsets), opens an oracle addressed to the exiles rather than to the courtyard men of Ezek.11.1-11.13 — an addressee-class shift inside the vision, from the Jerusalem claimants ('this land is given to us for a possession,' oshb:Ezek.11.15) to “your brothers… the house of Israel” (web:Ezek.11.15) in exile. The witness records a pe after MT 11:13 (single witness), at the seam this unit opens on at 11:14. Close: oshb:Ezek.11.21 וְאֶל לֵ֧ב שִׁקּוּצֵיהֶ֛ם וְתוֹעֲבוֹתֵיהֶ֖ם לִבָּ֣ם הֹלֵ֑ךְ דַּרְכָּם֙ בְּרֹאשָׁ֣ם נָתַ֔תִּי נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה ends with the utterance formula נאם אדני יהוה (one of the book's 81 utterance-close verses). Both sides are formula-clean: a strict word-event onset and an utterance close, the tightest formula bracket in this span. This embedded salvation oracle stands inside the still-open vision (the courtyard scene has not yet returned the prophet — that happens only at 11:22-25) but is bounded by its own onset and close formulae independent of the vision frame, so it is set as its own row rather than folded into 11:1-13 or 11:22-25.

It was not taken because 11:14 is a strict word-event onset (not a bare transition) and the oracle's own addressee — the scattered exiles — differs from the courtyard men addressed in 11:1-13, which is enough of a class shift to justify treating it as its own formula-bounded row even while the wider vision frame stays open around it.

boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.11.22 וַיִּשְׂא֤וּ הַכְּרוּבִים֙ אֶת כַּנְפֵיהֶ֔ם וְהָאֽוֹפַנִּ֖ים לְעֻמָּתָ֑ם וּכְב֧וֹד אֱלֹהֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם מִלְמָֽעְלָה resumes the vision frame exactly where 11:13 left it (the cherubim and wheels, last seen departing the city at 10:19). Close: oshb:Ezek.11.25 וָאֲדַבֵּ֖ר אֶל הַגּוֹלָ֑ה אֵ֛ת כָּל דִּבְרֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶרְאָֽנִי — “Then I spoke to the captives all the things that Yahweh had shown me.” (web:Ezek.11.25) — is the vision's own report-back close; a pe follows this verse (single-witness). This is the INTERNAL PARENT SEAM: oshb:Ezek.11.25 closes the transported vision that opened at 8:1, and oshb:Ezek.12.1 opens a plain word-event with no vision frame at all — the class shifts from vision report to oracle, which is why no row may run from one side of this seam to the other. Both sides: the close is double-marked (the return transport at 11:24 'the Spirit lifted me up… into Chaldea, to the captives' plus the pe after 11:25); the onset of oshb:Ezek.12.1 is a bare word-event with none of the vision devices that mark this vision's earlier scenes, which is the strongest possible contrast confirming the seam.
boundary_evidence_refs: oshb:Ezek.11.25 (pe follows; closes this row and the whole temple vision — the INTERNAL PARENT SEAM; single-witness)
oshb:Ezek.11.24 (vision.transport — the return “into Chaldea, to the captives” (web:Ezek.11.24); the vision “went up from me” (web:Ezek.11.24))
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this row to include oshb:Ezek.12.1 (reading the report-back and the fresh word-event as one continuous transition) was considered and rejected outright: 12:1 opens no vision device of any kind, and rows never straddle a parent seam. The four-verse length of this row is therefore not a granularity choice but the required stopping point before that seam.
literature_type_guess: the vision's return: the glory departs the city, the Spirit returns the prophet, and he reports to the exiles
device_notes: This row closes the P3 parent (the temple vision, oshb:Ezek.8.1-Ezek.11.25) at the seam between oshb:Ezek.11.25 and oshb:Ezek.12.1: the vision frame ends here, and oshb:Ezek.12.1 opens the P4 parent with a plain word-event carrying none of the vision's devices. Under-three-verse guard does not apply (this row is four verses) but the short length is disclosed as forced by the hard parent-seam stop rather than a free granularity choice. No K/Q or paseq falls in this span.

literature_type_guess: the Noah-Daniel-Job oracle: even these three could save only their own souls, applied to Jerusalem
device_notes: MT 14:14 and MT 14:20 both carry the Qere-adaptation editorial note class disclosed above, in addition to the ordinary ketiv/qere note at each verse (ketiv דנאל, qere דָּנִיֵּ֣אל (oshb:Ezek.14.14 and oshb:Ezek.14.20) — the shorter legendary-figure spelling against the fuller ‘Daniel’ reading); both disclosures are given at both verses since they are two independent single-witness apparatus facts about the same word. Paseq at 14:21 is count-only. oshb:Ezek.15.1 is cited above only as forward-side onset evidence for the seam; it is not a row here.
